en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Multiple myeloma is a malignancy of plasma cells (a type of white blood cell) in the bone marrow, associated with bone disease, renal impairment, anaemia and immunosuppression. In intensive care it is a comorbidity affecting infection risk, renal function and prognosis. Myeloma is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model (grouped with leukemia).

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *437233 / 109989006 — Multiple myeloma* with all descendants included, capturing multiple myeloma and its variants.

## Mapping Notes

- Leukemia and lymphoma are distinct haematologic malignancies captured by their own sets.

Vocabulary update: re-resolved against OMOP vocabulary v5.0 29-AUG-26 (previously v5.0 27-FEB-26).
19 → 14 concepts.

**Removed (4) — compound oncology concepts made non-standard by the OHDSI oncology remodelling; the diagnosis maps to a concept in the set, the qualifier (stage, subtype, remission/relapse, genetic finding) to Cancer Modifier, Episode or OMOP Genomic:**

- Multiple myeloma in remission (436059) → Multiple myeloma (437233) — in the set + Remission (32945, Episode) — outside the set
- Plasma cell leukemia in relapse (760936) → Plasma cell leukemia (133154) — in the set + Progression (32949, Episode) — outside the set
- Plasma cell leukemia in remission (133158) → Plasma cell leukemia (133154) — in the set + Remission (32945, Episode) — outside the set
- Relapse multiple myeloma (764229) → Multiple myeloma (437233) — in the set + Progression (32949, Episode) — outside the set

**Removed (1) — compound concepts made non-standard and split into their components:**

- Osteoporosis co-occurrent and due to multiple myeloma (42538151) → Multiple myeloma (437233) — in the set + Osteoporosis (80502) — outside the set
